covers: writing and describing ratios in colon notation, telling part-to-part from part-to-whole, and scaling a mix

intro.caption: Lesson 3-1 — understanding ratios. The qualifier is tonight, and Zara's hover-kart needs a new paint job: 2 parts blue to 5 parts white. One swapped number will ruin the whole look.

balloons.t: The livery calls for 2 parts blue to 5 parts white. Let's mix!
Ladies and gentlemen, Zara approaches the paint cans! Historic moment!
Wait. The order slip says 5:2 for blue to white. That's mostly blue!
Someone swapped the order. Blue comes first, so blue to white is 2:5.

pages.caption: A ratio compares two amounts, and the order matters. Blue to white is 2:5, not 5:2.

balloons.t: If you paint me 5 parts blue, I am calling the stewards. Fix that slip!
Two blue parts and five white parts make 7 total parts in one batch.
So 2:5 is part-to-part, and comparing white to all 7 is part-to-whole.
One batch won't cover the whole kart. We need 3 batches of the 2:5 mix.
Multiply both parts by 3, Beck. Do not eyeball it!
Final step: the trim stripe uses 3 parts teal to 4 parts chrome.
Four batches for the full stripe! Will the crew nail every ratio?
Even the paint job is faster than the Vipers! Now let's grab lunch!

win.caption: A ratio compares two quantities in a set order. Part-to-part compares two groups; part-to-whole compares one group to the total.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Write the Ratio
gates.prompt: Fix the paint shop order slip for Zara's 2 parts blue and 5 parts white mix.
hints: Conceptual: a ratio compares two quantities in the exact order the question names them.
Procedural: put the first named amount before the colon and the second named amount after it.

steps: Practice mix: 3 parts red to 4 parts silver.
Red is named first, silver is named second, so red to silver is 3:4.
If silver is named first, silver to red is 4:3.
worked.q: A stripe mix uses 4 parts gold to 7 parts black. Write gold to black.

items.q: Zara's livery uses 2 parts blue and 5 parts white. What is the ratio of blue to white?

options.fb: That swaps the order to white to blue. Blue is named first, so 2 goes first.
7 is the total parts, not the white paint. Blue to white compares the two paint parts.
That compares white paint to the total mix, not blue to white.

items.q: Which note on Beck's clipboard is actually a ratio?

options.t: There are 7 cans on the shelf
options.fb: That is only one count. A ratio must compare two quantities.
That describes the room without comparing two quantities.

options.t: 3 cans of teal for every 8 cans of silver

gates.pass: Slip fixed: 2:5 blue to white. Beck tosses the bad slip in the trash.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Part vs. Whole
gates.prompt: Use Lin's tape diagram for 2 parts blue and 5 parts white to compare part to whole.
hints: Conceptual: part-to-whole compares one part to the total of all parts together.
Procedural: add the parts first to find the total, then write part : total.

steps: Practice mix: 3 parts teal and 4 parts silver.
Part-to-whole ratio of teal to total mix is 3:7.
worked.q: A mix has 4 parts gold and 7 parts black. What is gold to total?

items.label: Total parts in one batch (2 blue + 5 white) =
items.aria: total parts in one batch of paint

fb.msg: That's 5 − 2. Total parts means adding all the parts together.
That's 2 × 5. Add the blue parts and white parts to get the total.
5 is only the white parts. Include the 2 blue parts too.

items.fbDefault: Add the 2 blue parts and the 5 white parts.

items.q: What is the part-to-whole ratio of white paint to the total mix?

options.fb: That is part-to-part (white to blue). Part-to-whole compares white to all 7 parts.
That is blue to total. Check which color the question asks for.
Order matters: white is named first, so 5 goes before 7.

gates.pass: 7 total parts, and 5:7 is white to whole. Spark approves.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Scale the Mix
gates.prompt: Beck needs 3 batches of the 2 blue : 5 white mix (7 total parts per batch).
hints: Conceptual: to keep the same color, every part and the total must grow by the same number of batches.
Procedural: multiply each amount in 1 batch by 3.

steps: Practice: 3 red to 4 silver (7 total parts).
For 2 batches, multiply each by 2: 3 × 2 = 6 red, 4 × 2 = 8 silver.
worked.q: For 2 batches of 1 gold to 3 black, how many parts black?

items.label: Blue parts in 3 batches (2 per batch) =

fb.msg: That added 2 + 3. Multiply 2 parts per batch by 3 batches.
15 is the white paint (5 × 3). Find the blue paint.
2 is only 1 batch. Beck needs 3 batches.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 2 blue parts per batch by 3 batches.

items.label: Total paint parts in 3 batches (7 per batch) =

fb.msg: That added 7 + 3. Multiply 7 parts per batch by 3 batches.
15 is only the white paint. Include the 6 blue parts too.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 7 total parts per batch by 3 batches.

gates.pass: 6 blue, 15 white, 21 parts in all. The sprayer is loaded.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Paint the Kart
gates.prompt: Lock in the trim stripe mix: 3 parts teal to 4 parts chrome (7 total parts).
hints: Conceptual: check the order of the words first, then check if it asks part-to-part or part-to-whole.
Procedural: for multiple batches, multiply the needed part by the number of batches.

steps: Practice trim: 2 yellow to 5 gray (7 total).
worked.q: In 1 red to 6 black, what is red to total?

items.q: What is the ratio of chrome to teal in the trim mix (3 teal, 4 chrome)?

options.fb: That's teal to chrome. Chrome is named first, so 4 goes first.
7 is the total. The question asks for chrome to teal.
That compares teal to the total mix.

items.q: What is the part-to-whole ratio of teal to the total trim mix?

options.fb: That is part-to-part (teal to chrome), not part-to-whole.
Order matters: teal comes first, so 3 goes before 7.
4:7 is chrome to total. The question asks for teal to total.

items.label: Chrome parts needed for 4 batches (4 per batch) =

fb.msg: That added 4 + 4. Multiply 4 parts per batch by 4 batches.
12 is the teal paint (3 × 4). Find the chrome paint.
28 is all 7 parts × 4. The question asks only for chrome.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 4 chrome parts per batch by 4 batches.

gates.pass: PSSSHHT! Clean teal and chrome stripes lock onto the fenders. Zara's kart is ready.

journal.heading: Lesson 3-1 — what the paint job taught us
rows: 2 parts blue to 5 parts white is 2:5. Swapping to 5:2 flips the colors.
Compares one part to another part, like 2 blue to 5 white (2:5).
Add the parts to find the total (2 + 5 = 7), then compare one part to the whole (5:7).
For 3 batches, multiply both parts by 3 so the color stays exact: 6 blue and 15 white.
journal.quote: "Swapping 2:5 into 5:2 is how you end up with a very confused hover-kart." — Spark

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-1 (Understand Ratios) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers ratio language, colon notation, order of terms, part-to-part vs. part-to-whole, and scaling batches.
standards: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities
